newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador leader under fire for 100 days of theatrics.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador leader under fire for 100 days of theatrics.

text.p: Ecuador's populist President Abdala Bucaram marked his 100th day in office on Monday under fire for his colourful antics and alleged failure to deal with his country's economic problems.

The "superhero of the poor," as Bucaram calls himself, has sung on stage at a beauty contest, flown warplanes, recorded a rock-'n'-roll CD and played soccer since becoming president, while accusing oil workers, Indians and teachers of being lazy and corrupt.
"The 100 days allow no room for optimism," ex-president Osvaldo Hurtado said. "Shouting, insulting, jumping, singing, flying ... what has that got to do with public issues?"
"Nobody is free from Bucaram's tongue. Three months are more than enough to know what this government is all about and what it will be," said another ex-president, Rodrigo Borja.

El Universo newspaper said in an editorial Bucaram was "heading for an abyss of failure that the Ecuadoran people do not deserve," adding: "In such a short time (Ecuador) has fallen into political crisis and economic uncertainty due to the negative propaganda the government inflicts against itself."
The 44-year-old president, who is facing two lawsuits for slander, was unperturbed by the barrage of criticism.
"In 15 years the previous governments could not solve hard problems like that of the energy and now 'The Madman' has to solve everything," Bucaram said recently, using his nickname.
His plan to fight inflation and poverty and foster economic recovery has been postponed several times but his government now plans to unveil its policies on Sunday.
